review.tagline: Python framework for programming LMs and optimizing their prompts and weights
review.summary: DSPy lets you describe LM-based systems as modular Python code instead of hand-written prompts. It includes optimizers that tune prompts and model weights against a metric, and targets classifiers, RAG pipelines and agent loops. It installs with pip; the README defers all usage details to dspy.ai.
review.audience: Python developers building and tuning LM pipelines, RAG and agents
strengths: Optimizers tune prompts and weights against a metric, including GEPA
Programs are composed as Python modules rather than prompt strings
Backed by published Stanford NLP research papers
weaknesses: README has no quickstart or code example; usage lives on the external docs site
Optimization needs a metric and example data, adding setup versus plain prompting
Supported model providers are not listed in the README
Library only: no UI, server or deployment tooling
